# Job Chapter 31 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 427v–428r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JOB_031_page_001.jpg, JOB_031_page_002.jpg

---

**1** "I made a solemn agreement with my eyes not to look at a young woman with lust.

**2** For what does God above have in store for such a person? What inheritance does the Almighty give from on high?

**3** Isn't it disaster for the wicked and ruin for those who do wrong?

**4** Doesn't God see everything I do? Doesn't he count my every step?

**5** Have I ever been dishonest? Have I ever rushed toward deceit?

**6** Then let God weigh me on honest scales — and he will see my integrity!

**7** If my feet have strayed from the right path, if my heart has followed where my eyes wandered, if any stain clings to my hands —

**8** then let someone else eat what I have planted, and let my crops be torn up by the roots.

**9** If my heart has been seduced by another woman, if I have lurked at my neighbor's door —

**10** then let my wife serve another man, and let others sleep with her.

**11** For that would be a disgraceful act, a crime deserving punishment.

**12** It would be a fire burning all the way to the grave, destroying everything I have.

**13** If I have ever denied justice to my male or female servants when they had a grievance against me —

**14** then what would I do when God confronts me? What could I answer when he calls me to account?

**15** Didn't the same God who made me in the womb also make them? Didn't the same One shape us all before birth?

**16** Have I ever refused to help the poor when they asked? Have I ever let a widow's hope die?

**17** Have I ever eaten my food alone, without sharing with the orphan?

**18** No — from the time I was young, I raised the orphan like a father, and from my earliest days I cared for the widow.

**19** If I have ever seen someone dying for lack of clothing, or a poor person with nothing to wear,

**20** and they did not bless me for warming them with wool from my sheep —

**21** if I have ever raised my hand against an orphan because I knew I had influence at the court —

**22** then let my arm be ripped from its socket; let my shoulder be torn from its joint.

**23** I could never do such things, because the dread of God's judgment held me back; I could not bear to face his majesty.

**24** Have I ever put my trust in gold or told fine gold, 'You are my security'?

**25** Have I ever gloated over my great wealth or taken pride in all that I earned?

**26** Have I ever gazed at the shining sun or the moon moving in its glory,

**27** and been secretly tempted to worship them, blowing them a kiss with my hand?

**28** That too would be a crime deserving judgment — for it would mean I had been unfaithful to God above.

**29** Have I ever celebrated when my enemy was ruined? Have I ever gloated when disaster struck him?

**30** No — I never let my mouth sin by calling down a curse on his life.

**31** Haven't the people in my household said, 'Everyone has eaten their fill at Job's table'?

**32** No stranger has ever slept in the street; I always opened my door to the traveler.

**33** Have I ever tried to hide my sins the way people do, concealing my guilt in my heart

**34** because I feared what people would think of me, because I was afraid of public shame, so that I stayed indoors and kept silent?

**35** If only someone would hear me! I have signed my name to my defense. Now let the Almighty answer me! Let my accuser put his charges in writing!

**36** I would wear that document on my shoulder with pride; I would bind it on my head like a crown.

**37** I would give God a full account of my life, step by step; I would approach him with the confidence of a prince.

**38** If my land itself cries out against me, if its furrows weep together —

**39** if I have taken its produce without paying, or worked its previous owners to death —

**40** then let thorns grow instead of wheat, and weeds instead of barley."

With this, Job's words come to an end.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**The most comprehensive ethical code in the ancient world:** Job 31 is a negative confession — a sworn oath of innocence covering virtually every aspect of moral life: lust (v.1), honesty (vv.5-6), adultery (vv.9-12), treatment of servants (vv.13-15), care for the poor, widows, and orphans (vv.16-23), greed (vv.24-25), idolatry (vv.26-28), vindictiveness (vv.29-30), hospitality (vv.31-32), hypocrisy (vv.33-34), and environmental stewardship (vv.38-40).

**v.15 — A revolutionary declaration:** "Didn't the same God who made me also make them?" This verse contains perhaps the most advanced concept of human equality in the ancient Near East. Job grounds the rights of servants not in social convention but in creation theology — all humans share the same divine origin.

**v.35 — The case rests:** Job has presented his evidence, sworn his oath, and signed his name. The ancient equivalent of "I rest my case." The ball is now in God's court. The silence that follows — filled by Elihu's speeches — only heightens the tension.

*— PNEUMA*
